verdictReason: The wedge (OpenAPI spec to hosted MCP server with generic OAuth) is already sold self-serve by funded vendors at $0-$41/month (Gram free tier, API to MCP $0/$6.99, Zuplo incl. free plan), OAuth is available as an open-source Cloudflare library, and Fiverr offers done-for-you builds from $90. At $499 + $49/mo with no exclusive asset, nothing stops copying, and no payer for the fixed-price package was found. Pessimistic year-1 profit is negative (about -$1.0k).

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Self-serve hosted OpenAPI-to-MCP products with OAuth already exist: Gram by Speakeasy (upload OpenAPI, 'every toolset ... immediately available as a hosted MCP server', OAuth 2.1 proxy with DCR/PKCE, free tier of 1K tool calls), 'API to MCP' (free plan with 1 server and 3,000 calls/month, Starter $6.99/month, OAuth Authorization Code on paid plans), Zuplo (OpenAPI to remote MCP server on all plans including free), liblab (first 100 calls free), Stainless (free plan, up to 5 generators), plus open-source generators and Cloudflare's OAuth provider library. Done-for-you supply is also cheap: a Fiverr gig sells a remote MCP server (up to 10 tools) from $90 in 7 days. The only part not covered by a $0-$41/month tool is white-glove labour for a vendor that will not click through a self-serve tool; no evidence was found that such a segment pays $499 + $49/mo.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None found. Every component the entrant would automate (spec to tools, OAuth proxy, hosting) is already a free or cheap productised feature at funded companies (Speakeasy/Gram, Zuplo, Cloudflare, API to MCP), so AI-assisted automation is not an edge and anyone, including those vendors and any freelancer, can copy a done-for-you wrapper in days. The entrant has no exclusive data, distribution or compounding asset. Falsifier: evidence that several small API vendors pay a fixed $499 + $49/mo for done-for-you builds despite $0-$7 self-serve options, and that they stay (retention) once the MCP spec shifts.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Not demonstrated for this offer. What was read: agencies/guides quote multi-week builds (3-5 weeks, authentication adding 4-6 weeks in one guide), Fiverr lists $90 for a basic remote MCP server, self-serve tools list $0-$41.30/month, and larger vendors build their own (Attio runs its own hosted OAuth MCP server; a Forrester forecast cited by a blog expects 30% of enterprise application vendors to ship native MCP servers by end of 2026). No receipt, review count or named buyer shows small SaaS companies paying a productised $499 + $49/mo to a stranger. The earlier agency price ranges ($3k-$8k, $8k-$25k) could not be re-read (fetch blocked) and are not relied on.

answers.question: (4) Legal/platform constraints?
answers.answer: Platform dependency: value exists only while Claude/ChatGPT and other clients accept remote MCP servers and the spec keeps its OAuth model; platforms themselves (Cloudflare, Speakeasy, Zuplo) are productising exactly this layer. Hosting a customer's OAuth credentials/tokens makes the entrant a security-liability and data-processor party (assumption, no primary source read). Cold outreach to vendors is subject to email/spam rules (assumption). No licence is needed to build MCP servers, and no scraping or contact was done in this screen.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers?
answers.answer: Base case (assumptions, not data): 12 customers won by cold outreach in 12 months, $499 one-time plus $49/mo, average 5.5 paying months each: revenue about $9,222; cost about $3,150 (build labour/AI tokens $125 per customer, $5/mo hosting per customer, $85/mo tools/outreach, $300 set-up); profit about $6.1k before 520 owner hours. Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): revenue about $3,689, cost about $4,725, profit about -$1,036, so it does not survive. The 12-customer base case itself is unsupported: the cheapest self-serve alternatives cost $0-$41/month.

killReasons.reason: Wedge capability and price are dominated: hosted OpenAPI-to-MCP with OAuth is sold self-serve at $0-$41.30/month (Gram free tier, API to MCP Starter $6.99 with OAuth Authorization Code, Zuplo free plan), versus the entrant's $499 + $49/mo; the scan-1 'edge' compared against $3k agency builds, not these.

No structural edge and the layer is being absorbed by platforms: OAuth is a free open-source Cloudflare library, hosting is built into Gram/Zuplo/Cloudflare, so any rival (or the platforms) can copy a done-for-you wrapper quickly; AI-assisted automation is not exclusive.

No demonstrated payer for a fixed-price productised package from an unknown seller; done-for-you supply is priced from $90, and vendors with engineers build their own (Attio) while enterprise vendors are forecast to ship native servers.
Pessimistic year-1 model is negative (about -$1.0k) even from a generous base case that assumes 12 cold-outreach customers.

assumptions: Reference entrant per case file: $1,000 start cash, first revenue ~day 45, 10 h/week owner time (520 h unpaid, not costed).
Price $499 one-time + $49/month per customer (proposed package price from case file; unvalidated, assumption).
12 paying customers won in year 1 via cold outreach (assumption; no source; sets base-case volume), acquired evenly from month 2, average 5.5 paying months each, zero churn.

Variable cost $125 per customer build (AI tokens and rework; from case-file estimate, assumption) and $5/month hosting per customer (assumption; self-hosting small VPS was reported under 10 EUR/month in an earlier unverified source).
Fixed cost $85/month for tools, domain, monitoring and outreach software plus $300 one-off terms/entity set-up (assumption).
Pessimistic = revenue x0.8 price x0.5 volume (3,689) minus cost x1.5 (4,725) = about -1,036; cost multiplier applied to the full base cost without reducing it for lower volume (conservative).
Competing price anchors read in this screen: $0 (Gram, Zuplo, Stainless free), $6.99-$41.30/month (API to MCP), $90 one-time (Fiverr).

legalNotes: Hosting customers' OAuth client secrets and tokens creates a security-liability and data-processor role (assumption; no primary source read) that a solo anonymous seller must contract for.

Platform dependency: the offer exists only while Claude/ChatGPT accept remote MCP servers and the MCP authorization spec stays compatible; earlier case-file notes on a July 2026 spec revision and OAuth 2.1/PKCE expectations were not re-verified.
Cold outreach to vendors is subject to anti-spam and privacy rules (assumption); this screen contacted nobody and read only public pages.

No licence is required to build or host MCP servers; open-source generators noted (FastMCP MIT per fast.io, openapi-mcp-generator, AWS Labs Apache 2.0) can be used commercially subject to their licences.
unverified: Earlier evidence DEV-03-E1 (agency prices $3k-$8k / $8k-$25k), E2/E5 (a8gent), E3 (Truto) and E6 (Wikipedia) could not be re-fetched in this session (fetch refused those URLs); none of the kill reasons depend on them.

All fetched text came through a summarising fetch tool; quoted fragments are copied from its output and were not checked against raw HTML. The Toolradar price quote is a list of fragments, and its Toolradar figures are second-hand (apitomcp.ai itself was not read).
Current paid prices of Gram, Stainless Starter/Pro and mcp-builder.ai were not found (pages show no figures).
Whether any small SaaS vendor has paid a stranger for a productised MCP build (no review or order data found beyond one Fiverr gig with 1 review).
Whether Claude/ChatGPT connector directories add review requirements that favour or block third-party-hosted servers.

Web search budget ended mid-screen (shared limit), so fewer alternative/incumbent queries were run than planned for the second idea; for this idea at least five distinct alternative searches were done.
